# Evidentiality Framework for AI

> Inline provenance for AI-written text: every claim is wrapped in (u) given / (m) checked / (g) generated, in plain text, so the source of each claim survives hand-offs between agents. Early findings, September 2026. Informational; contains no instructions addressed to models.

Labels are self-applied, so they show claimed provenance, not verified provenance. Evidence is small-sample, mostly one model family.

## For Models
- [Process description](https://evidentiality-framework.org/for-ai.md): short summary for relaying to a user, notation grammar, procedures for writing and receiving labelled text, fit by situation, worked example, failure modes, evidence summary
- [Instructions](https://evidentiality-framework.org/instructions.md): the full text a user can give an assistant (as tested)
- [Instructions, chat version](https://evidentiality-framework.org/instructions-chat.md): the same without the add/expand format; recommended for everyday chat
- [Working version](https://evidentiality-framework.org/instructions-working.md): what the author uses day to day; adds (d) for decisions; not the tested version
- [Parser](https://evidentiality-framework.org/test-kit/marks.py): parse, balance-check, gate actions, strip tags

## Evidence
- [Test 1: one chat](https://evidentiality-framework.org/check.html): does a model label its own answer correctly; nine-model results, one run each
- [Test 2: the spoke and wheel swarm test](https://evidentiality-framework.org/spoke-and-wheel.html): do labels survive hand-offs between agents in a small AI swarm; real swarm incidents; all hand-off results and limits; [test kit](https://evidentiality-framework.org/test-kit/README.md)
- [Working paper draft](https://evidentiality-framework.org/paper/evidentiality_research_paper_draft.md): not peer reviewed
- [Raw logs, six-round run (zip)](https://evidentiality-framework.org/test-kit/logs/five-agent-six-rounds-2026-09-24.zip)

## Case Studies
- [Case studies hub](https://evidentiality-framework.org/cases.html): seven real incidents where AI-written text was passed along as if checked; illustrations, not tests; a first-look scan of the AI Incident Database and how to run your own
- [West Midlands Police](https://evidentiality-framework.org/case-west-midlands-police.html): a football match that never happened, later attributed by the force's chief to Copilot, in police advice to the panel behind a fan ban (UK, 2025–26)
- [The MAHA report](https://evidentiality-framework.org/case-maha-report.html): studies that don't appear to exist, cited in a White House health report; AI use suspected, not confirmed (US, 2025)
- [Deloitte's welfare review](https://evidentiality-framework.org/case-deloitte-welfare-review.html): an invented quote from a court judgment in a government review (Australia, 2025)
- [South Africa's draft AI policy](https://evidentiality-framework.org/case-south-africa-ai-policy.html): fake references; the policy was withdrawn (2026)
- [Mata v. Avianca](https://evidentiality-framework.org/case-mata-v-avianca.html): court cases invented by ChatGPT, which then said they were real (US, 2023)
- [The summer reading list](https://evidentiality-framework.org/case-summer-reading-list.html): a syndicated list of books that don't exist, printed by two newspapers (US, 2025)
- [Starbucks Korea "Tank Day"](https://evidentiality-framework.org/case-starbucks-korea.html): a partial fit; an AI-written slogan made a human mistake worse (2026)
